title: Brain, Music and Learning Researchers Attend SysMus26 in Durham: Helsinki to Host SysMus27
content:
The Brain, Music and Learning Research Group was delighted to be represented at the 2026 International Conference of Students of Systematic Musicology (SysMus26), held in Durham, United Kingdom.

Two of our doctoral researchers, Cesc Bayle and Anni Tolvanen, attended the conference, joining an international community of early-career researchers working across musicology, psychology, neuroscience, education, technology, and related disciplines. SysMus provides a unique platform for doctoral researchers and students to share their work, exchange ideas, and build international collaborations in the field of systematic musicology.

Participation in SysMus26 offered valuable opportunities to engage with current research on music perception, cognition, learning, performance, and the many ways music intersects with human behavior and the brain. The conference also fostered meaningful discussions about emerging methodologies and future directions in interdisciplinary music research.

title: A summer of grants!
content:
Laura has been awarded a Una Europa mobility grant to support a research visit to Leiden University, where Assistant Professor Tuomas Aivelo hosted her. During the mobility period, Laura focused on developing her postdoctoral research plan, drawing on Leiden’s strong expertise and the collaborative opportunities within Tuomas’s group. Laura was there for eight days at the end of April 2026. During the visit, Laura also visited Naturalis and other museums in Leiden, which is known as the Museum Capital of the Netherlands. 

Gloria received a grant from Societas pro Fauna et Flora Fennica and from the Lammi Biological Station to support her field season and data collection. during the summer of 2026, she collected data from a wild population of pied flycatchers, recording provisioning rates and mobbing efforts of the parents.

content:

title: Sharing our research at 20th Annual FinPharmaNet meeting
content:
brought together doctoral researchers and the wider drug research community from across Finland on 20–21 August in Rauhalahti, Kuopio. The two-day meeting was a great chance to discover what other pharmacy units are working on, share ideas and, of course, meet fellow researchers from around the country.

Our group was well represented in the programme. Roya Khoshtinatnikkhoy gave a talk on Antibiotic-coated urinary catheters for prevention of catheter-associated urinary tract infections: Comparing dipping and impregnation coating strategies, presenting her work as part of the session on innovative formulation and drug delivery technologies.

On Friday, Maritta Keurulainen shared her work on Broccoli extract as a potential virulence inhibitor in uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) exploring whether broccoli extract could offer a new way of interfering with bacterial virulence. Daniel Wallinger presented his research on Metabolic adaptations in UPEC, looking at how bacterial metabolism could point towards new ways of tackling urinary tract infections.

The meeting ended on a particularly high note for Daniel, who won the Elevator Pitch Prize for his presentation.

title: Online Marketplaces Are Putting Biodiversity at Risk
content:
Researchers monitoring online activity for six weeks in mid-2025 advertised for sale across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. Like primates, birds, snakes, frogs, orchids, and many other wildlife groups are increasingly being trafficked through online platforms. Online illegal wildlife trade poses significant risks to species, ecosystems, and animal and public health.

A new study published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity by an international team of experts led by  from the University of Helsinki highlights that thousands of animal, plant, and fungal species, many of which are threatened with extinction, are being illegally traded online as global consumer demand continues to grow.

"The online illegal wildlife trade spreads across many platforms, including popular social media platforms, and represents a growing and evolving threat to biodiversity conservation," says Professor Di Minin. 

"What is particularly concerning is that many of the species found to be illegally traded online are either at high risk of extinction or had not previously been considered at risk from illegal wildlife trade," he continues.

title: Highlight of the month: Research on gambling disorder saves lives
content:
What a great opportunity to get to know one of Europe’s leading research groups in the field of gambling addiction!

My name is .  I am a health psychologist, university teacher, and PhD student. I am also a member of the (B17-23 R) at the and the . Our group is led by together with . Thanks to my university and , I was awarded an Erasmus+ grant that allowed me to undertake a short research stay at the Centre for Research on Addiction, Control and Governance at the University of Helsinki.

Allow me to introduce my research group. We have two main research lines: one focuses on mindfulness and the other on gambling, and it is within this latter area that I am developing my PhD thesis. From a gender perspective, we are developing the first preventive tool focused on gambling for women: , an app designed exclusively for women. This is where much of my group’s current work is concentrated, as well as a large part of my own work as a PhD student in psychology.

title: Tervetuloa Senaatintorille 24.8. osoittamaan tukea ukrainalaisille
content:
The UNITED FOR UKRAINE event, taking place on Ukraine’s Independence Day, Monday 24 August at 5pm at Senate Square, will celebrate vibrant Ukrainian culture through live music performances and a dance performance by Ukrainian children, while also expressing support for Ukraine’s independence and a lasting peace solution.

Greetings will be delivered by Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, Archbishop Tapio Luoma, and Deputy Mayor of Helsinki Johanna Laisaari. 

Sunflowers, Ukraine’s national flower, will be distributed to participants at the event.

At the end of the event at Senate Square, the Ukrainian community will form a large procession leading all interested participants along Aleksanterinkatu to Kansalaistori (Citizens’ Square), where the Ukrainian national anthem will be performed.

The UNITED FOR UKRAINE event is organized by the Evangelic Lutheran Church in Helsinki and the Association of Ukrainians in Finland in cooperation with the City of Helsinki, the University of Helsinki, the Prime Minister’s Office of Finland, and the Embassy of Ukraine.

title: Introducing Our New Newsletter: Bringing Canine Health Research, Education and Practice Together
content:
We are excited to introduce a brand-new newsletter created to bring together people who share one common interest: improving the health and wellbeing of dogs through knowledge, research and education.

The newsletter is a joint initiative between the DogRisk Research Group, the Raw Feeding Veterinary Society (RFVS) and the College of Integrative Veterinary Therapies (CIVT). By bringing together perspectives from research, veterinary practice and education, we hope to create a space where new knowledge can be shared across disciplines — and where scientific findings can reach the people who can put them into practice.

Each edition will feature a mix of research updates, expert articles, interviews, educational opportunities, upcoming events and news from our communities.

Our aim is to make the newsletter relevant to a wide audience. Whether you are a veterinarian, researcher, veterinary nurse, student, therapist, nutritionist, dog owner, or simply interested in learning more about canine health and nutrition, we hope you will find something worth reading.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Projects to Partnerships: HEP Programme Marked Its Final Chapter
content:
Organised by the Finnish National Agency for Education, the hybrid event brought together projects working across teacher education, sustainability, health sciences, and innovation partnerships. Rather than functioning simply as a closing event, the seminar became a space to reflect on how international higher education cooperation can continue beyond individual project cycles. All the presentations were broadcasted to an open audience on the YouTube channel of The Finnish National Agency for Education.

HEP-TED participated in the seminar’s thematic session on inclusive and future-ready teacher education together with the BERT, FUTE, and TIPOTE projects.

The session highlighted experiences from cross-institutional collaboration around learner-centred pedagogy, digital education, inclusion, and teacher education reform. Across the discussions, a common theme emerged: sustainable educational change requires long-term institutional cooperation rather than short-term interventions.
